notes_exact_visible_text: Put G(n,M)=gcd_{2<=a<=M}(a^n-1). If q|G(n,M), then q>M, and H={x in F_q^*:x^n=1} has at most n elements. For q>M^2, reduced fractions a/b, 1<=a,b<=M, inject into H. Their count is C(M)>=M^2/4+M, so M>=S(n) or C(M)>n gives a contradiction. For q<=M^2 and even n, Dirichlet gives x=a/k with 1<=k<=M and 0<|a|<M, so every x!=0 satisfies x^n=1; hence q-1|n, contradicting q>P(n). For odd n, all elements of H are squares and the least quadratic nonresidue is at most ceil(sqrt(q)), forcing q>M^2. Fermat gives P(n)<=h(n). The restriction is necessary: n=86 has P(n)=3 but h(n)=5.

summary_exact_visible_text: AI-assisted, Lean-formalized partial result for #770. Use the collective-gcd, strict-M>2 definition of h(n). Let P(n)=max{p prime:p-1|n} and S(n)=floor(sqrt(4n))+1. For every positive n, P(n)<=h(n)<=max{P(n),S(n)}, P(n)>2sqrt(n) implies h(n)=P(n). If n is odd, h(n)<=S(n). More sharply, if p=P(n)>2 and C(p)=#{(a,b):1<=a,b<=p,gcd(a,b)=1}>n, then h(n)=p, including cases with p<=2sqrt(n). These are partial results: the density, liminf, and general epsilon>0 questions remain unresolved. Novelty and priority have not been determined. AI disclosure: an OpenAI internal model.
